query: What additive manufacturing strategy and post-processing route can enable the fabrication of a refractory high-entropy alloy family (Group IV-V transition metals) capable of retaining high-temperature structural integrity, and what specific microstructural state is hypothesized to optimize mechanical performance while mitigating the inherent brittleness associated with interstitial impurities?

generation.hypothesis: A refractory high-entropy alloy (RHEA) based on the Nb-Ta-Zr-Mo-W system, fabricated via Laser Powder Bed Fusion (LPBF) followed by a two-stage heat treatment (solution annealing at 1400°C followed by aging at 900°C), will develop a dual-phase microstructure consisting of a BCC matrix and a coherent Laves phase precipitate, which optimizes high-temperature strength while the specific addition of 0.5 at.% Boron and 0.2 at.% Carbon during powder synthesis will segregate to grain boundaries to mitigate interstitial-induced brittleness.
generation.material_initial_state: Powders of Nb, Ta, Zr, Mo, and W with high purity (>99.9%) and controlled interstitial content (O < 500 ppm, C < 100 ppm, N < 50 ppm), mixed with trace amounts of elemental Boron and Carbon.
generation.intervention: Fabrication using Laser Powder Bed Fusion (LPBF) with a high scan speed and low hatch spacing to ensure rapid solidification, followed by a post-processing route involving solution annealing at 1400°C for 2 hours in vacuum, and subsequent aging at 900°C for 10 hours.
generation.conditions: Atmosphere: High vacuum (<10^-5 Pa) during LPBF and heat treatments; Temperature range: 25°C to 1200°C for mechanical testing; Strain rate: 10^-3 s^-1.
generation.structural_mediator: Coherent Laves phase (C14 or C15 structure) precipitates distributed within the BCC matrix, combined with Boron/Carbon segregation at the BCC grain boundaries.
generation.mechanism: The rapid solidification of LPBF suppresses the formation of brittle topologically close-packed (TCP) phases and refines the grain size, as demonstrated in W-Ta-Mo-Nb-V systems [PMC8201384::chunk::000::abstract::c39421387b]. The subsequent aging promotes the nucleation of coherent Laves phases that impede dislocation motion (precipitation hardening) without causing significant embrittlement, analogous to the 'stepwise controllable coherent nanoprecipitations' (SCCPs) strategy that enhances strength and ductility simultaneously [PMC10213035::chunk::000::abstract::2906c9eda2]. Simultaneously, the trace Boron and Carbon segregate to grain boundaries, strengthening the boundary cohesion and preventing the formation of brittle interstitial-rich phases, addressing the inherent brittleness of RHEAs [PMC8510135::chunk::001::introduction::e6ecd3ac9d].
generation.predicted_outcome: The resulting alloy will exhibit a yield strength exceeding 800 MPa at 1000°C and a tensile ductility of >10% at room temperature, significantly outperforming conventionally cast or unoptimized LPBF versions of the same alloy composition which typically suffer from catastrophic brittle failure due to interstitial segregation.
generation.baseline: Standard LPBF-fabricated Nb-Ta-Zr-Mo-W RHEAs without Boron/Carbon additions and without specific aging heat treatments, which typically exhibit high strength but near-zero ductility at room temperature and rapid strength degradation above 800°C due to grain boundary sliding and TCP phase formation.
generation.boundary: The hypothesis applies specifically to alloys with a nominal composition of Nb20Ta20Zr20Mo20W20 (at.%) with trace B/C additions; it may not hold for alloys with significantly different atomic size mismatches or valence electron concentrations that favor different crystal structures (e.g., FCC or HCP).
generation.uncertainty: There is uncertainty regarding the exact solubility limit of Boron and Carbon in the specific BCC matrix of this quinary system at the proposed aging temperature; excessive segregation could lead to the formation of brittle borides/carbides at grain boundaries rather than beneficial segregation, potentially reversing the ductility improvement.

falsification_experiment.design: Fabricate three sets of samples: (1) Baseline LPBF (no B/C, no aging), (2) LPBF + Aging (no B/C), and (3) LPBF + Aging + B/C addition. Perform tensile testing at room temperature and 1000°C. Conduct Atom Probe Tomography (APT) to analyze grain boundary chemistry.
measurements: Grain boundary composition profiles (B, C, O, N concentrations)
Phase identification via XRD and TEM
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: The hypothesis is falsified if the sample with B/C additions and aging shows a decrease in room temperature ductility below 5% or if APT analysis reveals the formation of continuous brittle boride/carbide networks at grain boundaries instead of discrete segregation, or if the aging treatment fails to produce the predicted Laves phase precipitates.

cited_evidence.text: Abstract High-performance refractory alloys with ultrahigh strength and ductility are in demand for a wide range of critical applications, such as plasma-facing components. However, it remains challenging to increase the strength of these alloys without seriously compromising their tensile ductility. Here, we put forward a strategy to “defeat” this trade-off in tungsten refractory high-entropy alloys by stepwise controllable coherent nanoprecipitations (SCCPs). The coherent interfaces of SCCPs facilitate the dislocation transmission and relieve the stress concentrations that can lead to premature crack initiation. As a consequence, our alloy displays an ultrahigh strength of 2.15 GPa with a tensile ductility of 15% at ambient temperature, with a high yield strength of 1.05 GPa at 800 °C. The SCCPs design concept may afford a means to develop a wide range of ultrahigh-strength metallic materials by providing a pathway for alloy design. Subject terms: Metals and alloys, Mechanical engineering

High entropy or multi principal element alloys are a promising and relatively young concept for designing alloys. The idea of creating alloys without a single main alloying element opens up a wide space for possible new alloy compositions. High entropy alloys based on refractory metals such as W, Mo, Ta or Nb are of interest for future high temperature applications e.g., in the aerospace or chemical industry. However, producing refractory metal high entropy alloys by conventional metallurgical methods remains challenging. For this reason, the feasibility of laser-based additive manufacturing of the refractory metal high entropy alloy W 20 Mo 20 Ta 20 Nb 20 V 20 by laser powder bed fusion (PBF-LB/M) is investigated in the present work. In-situ alloy formation from mixtures of easily available elemental powders is employed to avoid an expensive atomization of pre-alloyed powder. It is shown that PBF-LB/M of W 20 Mo 20 Ta 20 Nb 20 V 20 is in general possible and that a complete fusion of the powder mixture without a significant number of undissolved particles is achievable by in-situ alloy formation during PBF-LB/M when selecting favorable process parameter combinations. The requirements for designing novel metallic alloys that are capable of surpassing a whole set of specific properties of currently available commercial alloys are, at present, a subject of high demand in the industry. For instance, an improved combination of metallic alloys should possess strength and ductility while maintaining a relatively low cost. This is especially true when one is dealing with materials for high-temperature applications. Therefore, new engineering solutions are needed for novel materials that outperform the capabilities of the currently used Ni-based alloys. One of the prospective innovative materials that could be able to meet the requirements of such demanding applications, especially in the aviation and aerospace industries, may be refractory high-entropy alloys (RHEAs). These are also known by other names, such as complex concentrated alloys (CCAs). These materials have been extensively studied in recent years [ [1] , [2] , [3] , [4] , [5] , [6] , [7] ] due to their very interesting combination of properties in some of the compositions.
